QF.id: AIFM CIII Fee Structure and Fund Performance_8

question.text: Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III) has AUM of INR 500 cr and a daily volatility of 1.2%. Using parametric VaR with the standard 1.645 z-score, what is the 95% 1-day VaR?

explanation.text: The Logic: Parametric VaR, under the normal-distribution assumption, is computed as VaR = z × σ × AUM, where z is the standard-normal quantile for the chosen confidence level, σ is the period volatility, and AUM is the portfolio value. For a 95% 1-day VaR, the standard z-score is 1.645. Plugging in: VaR = 1.645 × 1.2% × 500 cr = INR 9.87 crore. Interpretation: under the model assumptions, there is roughly a 95% probability that the fund will not lose more than INR 9.87 crore in one day. The Trap: INR 13.96 cr uses z = 2.33, which corresponds to 99% confidence rather than 95%. INR 6 cr uses z = 1 (about 84% one-tailed confidence). INR 60 cr corresponds to a wildly large z-score with no standard interpretation. Picking the wrong z for the confidence level is a classic VaR error. Note: The cited NISM Series XIX-E workbook pages (193, 253, 319) define VaR conceptually but do not give the parametric VaR formula (z × σ × AUM) or the 1.645/2.33 z-score framework. The formula and framing above are general quantitative-finance knowledge rather than a workbook-page citation.
